fight: Does greater dispersion of investor horizons stabilise markets (more liquidity, lower fragility) or raise volatility?

claims: FMH ABM: stability rises from uniform to diversified horizons (with caveats at finite max horizon)
Higher cross-holder churn dispersion -> more liquidity, lower liquidity volatility (JFQA 2022)
Illiquidity premia depend on horizon heterogeneity
Crashes when horizon diversity shrinks (Li-Li-Sun 2017)
Mixed short/long populations raise return variability (LeBaron)
Heterogeneity of investments correlates with volatility on overlap networks (Forera et al. 2025)
CME's own simulated friction channel: more diversity, more volatility

evidence_quality_delta: Side A has the stronger empirical evidence (JFQA 2022 with a natural experiment; CME stock-level data agree); side B is mostly model-based.
scope_overlap: Partly scoped differently: side B is about mixing in a single market (more trading, more volume), side A about who can absorb whom in stress. Both can hold.

fight: In sell-offs, do long-horizon institutions absorb short-horizon selling within the same stock?

side_a.position: Yes: long-run investors supply outside liquidity
claims: Long-run investors supply outside liquidity (theory)
Long-term IO mitigated COVID losses (level)
Insurers/pensions trade countercyclically
Chan et al. argue long-horizon funds absorb fire-selling short-horizon funds (argued, not tested)

side_b.position: No: retail investors and arbitrageurs absorb; institutions amplify
claims: Retail, not long-horizon institutions, were the liquidity providers in the COVID crash
Investors trading against distressed funds (arbitrageurs) earn liquidity returns
Hedge funds trading against flows moderate fragility

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has direct trade-level evidence; side A is theory plus level correlations. Nobody has tested within-stock absorption by holder horizon.
scope_overlap: Genuine open question at the within-stock, by-horizon level: the gap Pivot B would fill.

fight: Is an institution's horizon a fixed trait or does it move (and could it move toward peers)?

claims: Trading frequency is an investor-specific fixed effect (Parsa)
Investors specialise by frequency in equilibrium; fund turnover highly persistent (Crouzet et al.)
Churn averaged over quarters to remove idiosyncratic shocks (Cella et al.)
Horizon mix evolves endogenously through performance/wealth selection (LeBaron)
Social interaction raises trading activity (Heimer; Gelman et al.) - retail
Horizon compression during crises (CME, measured on contaminated value-weight turnover)

evidence_quality_delta: Persistence evidence is strong; evolution evidence is model-based or retail. Project data: within-institution sd of log tau 0.55 vs total 0.92, AR(1) 0.75 (not a source; orchestrator diagnostic).
scope_overlap: Both can hold: a large fixed component plus a smaller time-varying part. Pivot A must explain the time-varying part.

fight: Can peer effects in a portfolio-overlap network be credibly identified with observational 13F data?

claims: Intransitive triads identify endogenous and exogenous effects (FoF IV)
Panel data, random shocks and structural models address correlated effects
Peers' idiosyncratic shocks as IV (Leary-Roberts; Georg et al.)
Outcome-on-group-mean regressions are vacuous (Angrist)
Exclusion bias with leave-out means and FE
FoF IVs weak in dense networks, invalid in sampled networks

evidence_quality_delta: Both sides are methodological and correct within scope; side B sets the bar side A must clear.
scope_overlap: Not a disagreement about truth: a checklist. The top-150 sample makes the sampled-network critique bite; full 13F universe fixes it.

fight: Is price-drift contamination of turnover-based horizons a new finding?

side_a.position: CME: value-weight turnover is contaminated; share-based removes the VIX link
claims: CME project result r=-0.53 -> -0.06

side_b.position: Already handled by the standard measures
claims: GMM churn nets out passive price changes
Yan-Zhang churn price-adjusted numerator
Modified Turnover vs buy-and-hold weights
Zhu, Chen-Lee-Sun use the same correction

fight: Are short-horizon institutions destabilising or informed/beneficial?

claims: Short-term IO drives crash risk
High-turnover top institutions -> volatility
Short-horizon sell more in turmoil
Stock duration predicts idio vol
Short-term institutions' trades forecast returns
Short-horizon investors help firms adapt
Short-horizon institutions drive ownership-valuation link

scope_overlap: Scoped differently (stability vs information). Both right.

fight: Is the Fractal Market Hypothesis empirically testable at the investor level?

claims: FMH predictions fit index behaviour in GFC

side_b.position: Investor horizons not identifiable from data (2014 view)
claims: Real data cannot identify horizons, so ABM results untested

evidence_quality_delta: Weak on both sides; holdings-based horizons answer side B.
